holes_addressed: WIN-066.c6 hole #2 / c5 hole #1 (minor, carried forward): Counter (1) appeals to globe-physics mechanisms (NH ~39% land vs SH ~19% land; albedo asymmetry; aerosol-radiation forcing) without making explicit why those inputs are not themselves contested under the globe/dome dispute. A sophisticated dome defender could call the original Counter (1) circular: "you are using globe physics to refute the dome." The fix reframes Counter (1) as appealing to three directly-observable empirical inputs (continental land coverage; CERES-measured albedo; aerosol-radiation chemistry) and names each as geometry-neutral, with the strongest move being the consistency-trap on CERES: the dome model already accepts the CERES +0.34 W/m²/decade figure as its source of confirmation, so it cannot consistently reject CERES-derived surface-albedo measurements without forfeiting its own claimed WIN.
new_evidence_added: Explicit geometry-neutrality claim for the three Counter (1) inputs: continental coverage = geographic mapping (true under any rotational-pole-centered projection); surface albedo = CERES satellite product = same instrument the dome cites for +0.34; aerosol-radiation chemistry = atmospheric chemistry, not a geometric derivation. No new sources added (the existing Loeb 2025 citation is retained and now explicitly anchors the third input).

CERES consistency trap: making it explicit that disowning CERES-measured surface albedo while owning CERES-measured TOA flux is a position no self-consistent dome cosmology can hold. This was implicit in the prior text (Counter 3 used a similar own-it-or-disown-it dilemma for the inverse-cube integral); the patch makes Counter (1) carry the same structural move.

anticipated_objections.objection: Continental coverage IS projection-dependent on a dome: under an azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the NP, the SH appears as an annular ring with greater area density. The dome defender can recompute "~19% SH coverage" as a larger fraction under their preferred projection and argue your "geographic measurement" is itself a globe artifact.
anticipated_objections.response: Coverage percentages here refer to fraction of total land surface (NH-half vs SH-half of the rotational sphere), not fraction of any 2D map area. Land bodies are physical objects with measured boundaries; their distribution into hemispheres is a fact about where they sit relative to the equator, independent of any 2D projection used to display them. globe-fingerprints/WIN-066.json explicitly distinguishes the AE area ratio (1:3) from the land-mass distribution we cite here, and the over-prediction critique survives under either mapping (as the curmudgeon c6 stronger_arguments[1] notes). The clearer move would be to name "land surface area inventory" instead of "continental coverage," but the current phrasing is consistent with the standard climatological convention.

anticipated_objections.objection: The CERES consistency-trap framing is itself a debater move, not a scientific argument. If a defender simply says "I disown CERES too, and reframe the +0.34 as a coincidence I no longer cite," the trap closes on empty space.
anticipated_objections.response: That retreat is exactly the Counter (3) dilemma already in the text ("Either the dome predicts a magnitude and is wrong by ~250-800×, or it predicts only sign and the +0.34 coincidence is content-free"). A defender who disowns the +0.34 figure has abandoned the WIN entirely — there is then no NH heat excess asymmetry "confirmation" left for them to claim. The CERES consistency-trap is rhetorically supplementary to Counter (3), not load-bearing on its own; it tightens Counter (1) without replacing the structural Counter (3) move.

anticipated_objections.objection: You are still using globe-physics terminology ("hemispheres," "surface albedo," "aerosol-radiation interactions"). A radical dome defender could insist all of these are theory-laden, not direct measurements.
anticipated_objections.response: The reductio is too strong: under that standard, no observational claim is ever "direct" because every measurement is interpreted through some model. The relevant question is whether the inputs are theory-neutral *between* globe and dome cosmology, not whether they are theory-free in some absolute sense. Continental boundaries (mapped by direct survey), satellite-measured radiance (a CERES detector reading, processed under physics common to globe and dome geometries), and aerosol chemistry (laboratory results on light-scattering by atmospheric particles) are all theory-neutral between the two cosmologies under dispute — a dome model that uses CERES output cannot consistently reject the same instrument's albedo retrievals.

kernel_of_truth: The original Counter (1) does correctly identify the three independent mechanisms (land-mass differential, albedo asymmetry, aerosol forcing) and correctly anchors them in Loeb et al. 2025 — using the dome's own implicitly-accepted source against the dome's WIN claim. That structural move was sound. What it missed was making explicit that none of the three inputs is itself a globe-geometry derivation, leaving a sophisticated dome defender room to charge circularity. The patch preserves the original three-mechanism appeal and the Loeb 2025 anchor while inserting one named-and-classified empirical-anchor framing and a CERES consistency-trap. The Loeb 2025 source remains the most cited element because it is the dome's own implicit source of confirmation.
